newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins dawdle ahead of U.S. Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins dawdle ahead of U.S. Fed meeting.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds were little changed on Tuesday as the market bided its time ahead of dealers' talk of a possible U.S. interest rate hike later today.

"It has been the second day of no activity," a Deutsche Morgan Grenfell dealer in Moscow said. "Everybody is waiting for the results of the (FOMC) meeting. If anything, prices would move just one-eighth of a point."
The U.S. policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets at 1300 GMT and could raise U.S. interest rates. The Fed generally announces its decision around 1815 GMT.
In a Reuters survey, a slight majority of U.S. primary dealers believed the Fed would keep key rates unchanged.

MinFins, along with other emerging market debt, are sensitive to any news of a rise in U.S. interest rates, as such news usually pushes down U.S. Treasury bond prices. MinFins usually track U.S. Treasuries.
A Russian dealer said local banks were reluctant to do anything without seeing how markets in Western Europe and the United States would react to whatever Fed news emerges.
"Who knows what we will come to tomorrow -- it is better not to open any positions," the dealer said.
